citation: Adaptive urban economies: evidence of intra-day temporal behavioural adaptation to extreme heat in Australian cities
data: Bank card transactions (Westpac ~21% share) + airport max-temp
method: Fixed-effects panel regression across 6 daily time-blocks with lead-lag
key_finding: Heat >=35C collapses midday (12-6pm) spending 8-9.4% while morning/evening hold; behaviour shifts in TIME not just place
limitations: Proprietary card data; Australian context; online txns excluded; behavioural not tourist-specific
transferability_to_madrid: Concept transfers (temporal shifting); DATA does not - no equivalent open card data for Madrid tourists. Use as justification for time-slice unit, NOT as method

citation: CoolWalks for active mobility in urban street networks
data: OSM street network + building footprints/heights (Spanish Cadastre, NYC)
method: Route-choice model with sun-aversion parameter; CoolWalkability metric; 2.5D shadow model
key_finding: Shade-based routing benefit depends on building-height variation and street irregularity; on a regular grid CoolWalkability is independent of sun-aversion
limitations: Fixed sun position; no empirical pedestrian preferences; simplified constant building heights; sidewalk data gaps
transferability_to_madrid: HIGH THREAT: already covers Spanish cities with cadastre HATI would use. Confirms routing frontier is saturated; HATI must NOT frame as routing

citation: Mitigating Heat Stress by Reducing Solar Exposure in Pedestrian Routing
key_finding: Routing that penalises solar exposure yields materially cooler paths at modest distance cost
limitations: Assumes exposure model; no behavioural validation
transferability_to_madrid: Method transferable but competes on saturated frontier; useful as comparator not core

citation: Walking smart in the heat: a dynamic shade-oriented pathfinding approach to enhance pedestrian comfort in arid cities
key_finding: Time-dependent shade routing outperforms static shade routing as sun moves
limitations: Arid-climate case; computational; no field behavioural test
transferability_to_madrid: Reinforces routing saturation; time-dependence idea relevant to time-slice framing

citation: Cool routes: real-time human thermal exposure routing
method: Real-time thermal-exposure routing with hourly forecasts
key_finding: Real-time, forecast-driven cool routing reduces walking heat exposure
limitations: No tourism suitability layer; routing only
transferability_to_madrid: Confirms even real-time routing is now done; HATI differentiates upstream (suitability, not path)

citation: Active route choice to minimize pedestrian thermal discomfort in a high-density subtropical city
key_finding: Route choice can meaningfully cut cumulative thermal discomfort
transferability_to_madrid: Method transferable; again routing-frontier, not HATI's object

citation: Is satellite land surface temperature an appropriate proxy for intra-urban variability of daytime heat stress?
key_finding: Satellite LST is an inadequate stand-alone proxy for intra-urban daytime human heat stress
transferability_to_madrid: CORE justification for HATI's LST!=comfort rule; cite to defend not using raw LST

citation: Beyond land surface temperature: identifying areas of daytime thermal discomfort in cities by combining remote sensing and field measurements
method: Fusion of RS with in-situ to map discomfort
key_finding: Combining RS with field data identifies discomfort areas that LST alone misses
transferability_to_madrid: Directly informs HATI validation design (RS + reference)

citation: Comparative reliability assessment of PET and UTCI thermal comfort indices using Monte Carlo simulation in urban microclimates
method: Monte Carlo uncertainty on PET vs UTCI
key_finding: PET and UTCI differ in reliability/sensitivity; index choice carries quantifiable uncertainty
transferability_to_madrid: Justifies HATI's uncertainty propagation and index-choice caution

citation: A framework for heat risk action planning for tourism
key_finding: Provides governance framing for tourism heat risk and adaptation planning
transferability_to_madrid: High relevance for framing and policy positioning; complements HATI's technical layer

citation: Climate change and tourism demand: risks for extreme heat?
key_finding: Extreme heat poses material risk to tourism demand under warming
transferability_to_madrid: Background/motivation; not method

citation: Tourism in a warming climate: tourist experiences and adaptive responses to rising temperatures in Southern Europe destinations
key_finding: Tourists in Southern Europe already adapt experiences/timing to heat
transferability_to_madrid: Geographically apt (S. Europe); supports adaptation premise, not behaviour prediction

citation: Impact of high temperatures on tourist flows in urban and rural areas: climate adaptation strategies in China
key_finding: High temperatures redistribute tourist flows between urban and rural areas
transferability_to_madrid: Concept only; DATA basis (flow data) unavailable for Madrid tourists

citation: Heatwaves reduce intra- and intercity human mobility
key_finding: Heatwaves reduce human mobility within and between cities
transferability_to_madrid: Concept supports exposure logic; data not replicable openly for Madrid tourists

citation: Extreme heat reduces and reshapes urban mobility
key_finding: Extreme heat both reduces and spatially reshapes urban trips
transferability_to_madrid: Motivates spatial reshaping premise; not a usable data source

citation: Mobilities in the heat: identifying travel-related urban heat exposure and its built-environment drivers using remote sensing and mobility data in Chengdu
method: RS-mobility fusion for travel heat exposure
key_finding: Built-environment drivers of travel heat exposure identifiable by fusing RS and mobility
transferability_to_madrid: Closest methodological cousin; shows the version HATI CANNOT do without mobility data - useful contrast

citation: Are Barcelona's climate shelters accessible to vulnerable residents? A mobility justice analysis
key_finding: Climate-shelter accessibility is uneven across vulnerable resident groups
transferability_to_madrid: Directly transferable method; HATI extends the frame from residents to visitors in Madrid

citation: Measuring the attractiveness of trip destinations based on human mobility data
key_finding: Destination attractiveness can be quantified from observed mobility
transferability_to_madrid: Attractiveness-from-behaviour approach unavailable to HATI; use POI/static proxy instead and say so

citation: Identifying tourism attractiveness based on intra-destination tourist behaviour: evidence from Wi-Fi data
key_finding: Intra-destination attractiveness inferable from Wi-Fi behavioural traces
transferability_to_madrid: Shows behavioural attractiveness needs data HATI lacks; supports static-proxy honesty

citation: Risk of mortality and disease attributable to the heat stress index and its variability during heat waves: an observational study on the city of Madrid
key_finding: Heat-stress index and its variability predict mortality/disease risk in Madrid heatwaves
transferability_to_madrid: MADRID-specific; anchors local heat severity and index relevance

citation: Exploring 130 years of temperature-related mortality in the city of Madrid
key_finding: Long-run, rising temperature-mortality burden documented for Madrid
transferability_to_madrid: MADRID-specific motivation; establishes problem severity

citation: Heat-related mortality in Europe during 2024 and health emergency forecasting to reduce preventable deaths
key_finding: Tens of thousands of heat-related deaths in Europe 2024; forecasting can reduce them
transferability_to_madrid: Macro motivation and stakes; not method

citation: Shade for pedestrians: a novel approach to calculate the spatio-temporal shade benefits of street trees considering pedestrian flow
key_finding: Street-tree shade benefit is spatio-temporal and flow-weighted
transferability_to_madrid: Shade-modelling method transferable; flow-weighting optional and data-limited for Madrid

citation: Maximizing the pedestrian radiative cooling benefit per street tree
key_finding: Tree placement can be optimised for pedestrian radiative cooling
transferability_to_madrid: Foundational shade/MRT method for HATI exposure layer

citation: spanishoddata: a package for accessing and working with Spanish open mobility big data
journal: Environment and Planning B: Urban Analytics and City Science
key_finding: Provides reproducible open access to Spanish population mobility (MITMA) OD flows
limitations: Population-level, NOT tourist-specific; district granularity; privacy aggregation
transferability_to_madrid: Best accessible mobility proxy for Spain; supports CONTEXT only, cannot isolate tourists - key feasibility boundary

citation: Analysis of urban heat island and heat waves using Sentinel-3 images: a study of Andalusian cities in Spain
key_finding: Sentinel-3 usable for Spanish urban UHI/heatwave detection at coarse resolution
transferability_to_madrid: Spanish RS precedent; too coarse for pedestrian scale - informs resolution limits

citation: Urban heat island effect: remote sensing monitoring and assessment - methods, applications and future directions
key_finding: Synthesises RS-UHI methods and gaps; flags scale/validation limits
transferability_to_madrid: Method map and caveats for HATI RS layer

citation: Evaluation of the surface urban heat island effect in the city of Madrid by thermal remote sensing
key_finding: Characterises Madrid surface UHI structure from thermal RS
transferability_to_madrid: MADRID baseline for SUHI; foundational local reference

citation: Weights and importance in composite indicators: closing the gap
key_finding: Nominal weights in composite indicators rarely equal their actual importance; results are weight-sensitive
transferability_to_madrid: CORE justification for AVOIDING an arbitrary-weight composite tourism score

citation: Uncertainty and sensitivity analysis as tools for the quality assessment of composite indicators
journal: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
key_finding: Composite indicators require formal uncertainty/sensitivity analysis to be credible
transferability_to_madrid: Mandates HATI's sensitivity/uncertainty step if any aggregation is used

citation: An uncertainty and sensitivity analysis approach for GIS-based multicriteria landslide susceptibility mapping
journal: International Journal of Geographical Information Science
key_finding: GIS-MCDA rankings are sensitive to criteria/weights; sensitivity analysis is essential
transferability_to_madrid: Template for HATI's spatial sensitivity analysis regardless of domain
